chunks: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from his father from Abi Talib al-Sha'rani from Sulayman ibn Mu'alla ibn Khunays from his father who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man, and I was with him. It was said, 'Need has befallen him.' He said, 'What is he doing today?' It was said, 'In the house, worshipping his Lord, Exalted and Glorious.' He said, 'Then from where is his sustenance?' It was said, 'From some of his brothers.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'By Allah, the one who provides his sustenance is more devoted in worship than he is.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for providing financial sustenance to a worshipper?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the status of the provider (*muqtid*) above that of the secluded worshipper, establishing that facilitating another’s ability to worship is a superior act of devotion. This insight underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the social and economic dimensions of faith, where earning and sustaining the community are viewed as active, continuous worship (*ibadah*) rather than mere worldly necessity. It challenges the notion of ascetic isolation, affirming that practical support for believers holds immense spiritual weight.
